new.title: Peer through the window of the Inkijkmuseum
new.desc: One of the smallest museums in the country sits in the old rinsing house of a linen factory. You never go inside: the changing exhibition is arranged so you look at it through the windows, day or night.
new.tip: Swing by after dark on your way to or from the Effenaar; the lit display window is at its best then.

new.title: Walk around The Blob on 18 Septemberplein
new.desc: Massimiliano Fuksas shaped this steel and glass shopping building from a lump of clay he dented with his fists. Its smaller twin, the Bubble, joined it across the square a few years later.
new.tip: Stand by the stairs down to the underground bike park; from there you see both the Blob and the Bubble in one frame.

new.title: Spot the Philips radio in Eindhoven Centraal
new.desc: The 1956 station building is said to be modelled on a Philips tube radio, with the clock tower as its tuning knob. A long renovation kept the outside almost untouched.
new.tip: Look at it from across Stationsplein rather than from up close; the radio shape only clicks at a distance.

new.title: Look up at the tree tower of Strijp-S
new.desc: The Trudo Toren is a vertical forest of social housing, with trees and shrubs growing out of every balcony. It brought Milan's famous Bosco Verticale idea to an old Philips factory site.
new.tip: Next door, an orange housing block seems to hop over the Area 51 skate park; look at both from Ketelhuisplein.

new.title: Pass through the kasbah gate of Volta Galvani
new.desc: Behind a big gate with a lamp hanging over it hides a courtyard of brightly painted houses that feels more Mediterranean than Brabant. It was the first renewed corner of Woensel-West, named after the inventors of the battery and galvanism.
new.tip: Continue onto Edisonstraat afterwards: the WestSide Stores there are a row of independent boutiques and vintage shops.

new.title: Sit behind the wheel at the DAF Museum
new.desc: Hub van Doorne opened a small smithy on Tongelresestraat in 1928, and the trucks and cars of DAF grew out of it. The museum stands on that very spot, full of trucks, little DAF cars with their famous automatic gearbox, and prototypes.
new.tip: Begin in the restored forge at the start of the tour; some of the vehicles further on you are allowed to climb into.

new.title: Graze your way through Downtown Gourmet Market
new.desc: A food hall at the foot of the Vestedatoren with around twenty small kitchens from all over the world under one roof. Everyone in the group can eat something different and still sit together.
new.tip: Grab a table first and then split up; at peak dinner time on Fridays and Saturdays seats go before the food does.
new.q: Downtown Gourmet Market Smalle Haven Eindhoven

new.title: Try an odd ice cream flavour at Intelligentia
new.desc: This bright pink ice cream parlour under the Leidingstraat pipes is known for flavour combinations you would not dream up yourself. It fits right in with Strijp-S's experimental mood.
new.tip: Ask to taste the strangest flavour of the day before you pick; the staff are happy to let you try.

new.title: Lunch among the furniture at Piet Hein Eek
new.desc: Designer Piet Hein Eek turned the old Philips radio and TV factory on Strijp-R into workshop, shop, gallery and restaurant in one. You eat with a view of the scrapwood furniture being made.
new.tip: Walk through the workshop and gallery after lunch; you can watch the makers at work through the windows.

new.title: Have a drink at FIFTH on the old gasworks
new.desc: On the former NRE gasworks site, just east of the centre, this restaurant and bar is a local favourite with live music and its own roasted coffee. It feels far from the busy streets though it is a short walk away.
new.tip: Check the agenda for live music nights; the terrace among the old gasworks buildings is the place to be on summer evenings.

new.title: Eat seasonal at Frank in Woensel-West
new.desc: A neighbourhood restaurant on Franklinplein that cooks homestyle, vegetable-led dishes that follow the seasons, with natural wines to match. It is the kind of place locals keep to themselves.
new.tip: Combine it with a stroll past the coloured houses of Volta Galvani and the shops on Edisonstraat.
new.q: Frank Eten en Drinken Franklinplein Eindhoven

new.title: Do a silly walk through the Dommel tunnel
new.desc: The pedestrian and bike tunnel under the railway is painted with John Cleese's civil servant from Monty Python's Ministry of Silly Walks, step by absurd step. Cleese himself came to open it in 2016.
new.tip: Film a friend doing their best silly walk along the full length of the wall; everybody does it.

new.title: Travel 10,000 years at Museumpark VONK
new.desc: The new museum park in the Genneper Parken joins the open-air preHistorisch Dorp with the Eindhoven Museum collection. You can help build things in the workshop, watch old crafts and walk over the green roof of the biobased museum building.
new.tip: Park at Anton Coolenlaan and walk the last stretch through the Genneper Parken; combine it with the Genneper Watermolen nearby.

new.title: Hunt for sculptures in the Stadswandelpark
new.desc: South of the centre, this leafy park along the Dommel is dotted with modern and contemporary sculptures. It is where Eindhovenaren go for a quiet Sunday walk.
new.tip: Enter from the Wilhelminaplein side and follow the water; most sculptures are along the paths near the ponds.

new.title: Watch the windmills turn on Heusden's walls
new.desc: The star-shaped fortress town of Heusden on the Bergsche Maas is one of the best-preserved in the country. Three grain mills on its ramparts once kept the town fed during sieges.
new.tip: Come on the first Saturday of the month, when the millers set the sails turning and open up. From Den Bosch, bus 135 stops close to the old town.

new.title: Find the other cube houses in Helmond
new.desc: Everyone knows Piet Blom's tilted cube houses in Rotterdam, but Helmond had them first: the trial cubes went up here in 1974. Eighteen cubes still cluster around the site of the 't Speelhuis theatre, which burned down in 2011.
new.tip: Walk on to Kasteel Helmond in the Warande park, five minutes away; you can look at the moated castle for free from the park.

new.title: Explore the marquises' palace in Bergen op Zoom
new.desc: The Markiezenhof, begun in 1485, is one of the oldest and finest city palaces in the Low Countries, with a carved chimneypiece in its great hall. It also tells the story of the Bergse Vastenavend, the town's wild carnival.
new.tip: Climb to the attic for the old fairground collection, then walk to the Gevangenpoort, the only surviving city gate.

new.title: Visit the margarine villa of Museum Jan Cunen in Oss
new.desc: Oss grew rich on margarine, and this neoclassical villa was built in 1888 for a son of margarine maker Simon van den Bergh. Today it houses an art museum with Hague School paintings and modern work.
new.tip: The museum cafe and garden terrace in the newer wing are a good stop even after a short visit. The station is a ten minute walk away.

new.title: Sit under the Boterlinde on Eersel's Markt
new.desc: Eersel, the 'pearl of the Kempen', has an oval market square laid out for farm carts, lined with old inns and a Gothic chapel from 1464. Farm women once sold butter under the dome-shaped Boterlinde lime tree.
new.tip: Listen for the carillon in the old town hall every half hour, and pop into the Kempen regional museum De Acht Zaligheden.

new.title: Discover Roosendaal's past in the Tongerlohuys
new.desc: This elegant 1762 house was a refuge of the Belgian abbey of Tongerlo, from where its priests ran the local parish while Catholic worship was banned in public. Now it is the city museum of Roosendaal.
new.tip: Look for the Louis XV door frames and the original stucco ceilings before heading into the exhibitions.

new.title: Hunt for murals of Blind Walls Gallery in Breda
new.desc: More than 80 large murals by Dutch and international artists cover blank walls all over Breda, making the city an open-air street art gallery that costs nothing to visit.
new.tip: Use the Blind Walls app or map to build your own route, or rent a bike: the walls are spread far beyond the old centre.

new.title: See Kapoor's Sky Mirror at De Pont in Tilburg
new.desc: Tilburg's contemporary art museum fills a former wool-spinning mill, and you can still sense the factory in its big halls. Anish Kapoor's Sky Mirror reflects the clouds at the entrance.
new.tip: Entry is free on Thursday evenings and for visitors under 26; it is a short walk from Tilburg station.

new.title: Taste Trappist beer at Koningshoeven
new.desc: Monks of the Koningshoeven abbey in Berkel-Enschot, on the edge of Tilburg, have brewed beer since 1884. La Trappe is the only Dutch Trappist you can drink at the abbey itself.
new.tip: Book a brewery tour, then sit in the proeflokaal (tasting room); from Tilburg it is about 20 minutes by bike.

new.title: Eat a pancake inside Heusden's fortress walls
new.desc: After a walk over the ramparts and past the harbour, De Pannenkoekenbakker on the Vismarkt is where visitors to Heusden refuel with a proper Dutch pannenkoek.
new.tip: Ask for a spek (bacon) pancake with stroop (syrup) to drizzle on top, the way the Dutch eat it.

new.title: Have Persian ice cream at the Piushaven
new.desc: Tilburg's old industrial harbour is now its liveliest waterfront, with terraces along the quay and a bridge that swings sideways. By the bridge, the little Karvansara caravan serves Persian ice cream and tea.
new.tip: Walk the full loop along the quay, about one and a half kilometres, and finish with ice cream by the bridge.

new.title: Eat at the old feed mill of De Noordkade in Veghel
new.desc: A huge former animal feed factory on the canal in Veghel is now a food and culture hub with street art. At De Afzakkerij you eat where sacks of feed were once filled.
new.tip: Ask about a table at Sillyfox, 32 metres up in the old silo, for the view over the Brabant fields.

new.title: Pick a dinner at Foodmarket Tilburg
new.desc: In the Spoorzone next to the station, this food hall gathers more than a dozen kitchens in an old railway building, with trains rolling past.
new.tip: Combine it with an afternoon at the LocHal and a climb of the Kempentoren lookout in the Spoorpark across the tracks.

new.title: Celebrate carnival in Oeteldonk
new.desc: For carnival Den Bosch becomes Oeteldonk, the frog marsh, and the whole city dresses in a farmer's smock (boerenkiel) with a red, white and yellow scarf. The Prince arrives at the station at 11:11 on Sunday and the statue of Knillis rises on the Markt.
new.tip: Wear the real outfit, kiel, scarf, red handkerchief and white mittens; costumes from elsewhere stand out here.

new.title: Sail under the city on the Binnendieze
new.desc: Den Bosch's old waterways run beneath houses, streets and fortress walls. A silent boat takes you through tunnels and past medieval cellars, with a guide telling the story of the swamp dragon city.
new.tip: Book ahead for weekends and check which pier your ticket uses, Molenstraat or Zuidwal; online maps can send you to the wrong spot.

new.title: Cross the Moses Bridge at Fort de Roovere
new.desc: Near Halsteren, close to Bergen op Zoom, a sunken wooden bridge cuts through the moat of a 17th century earthen fort, so you walk between two walls of water.
new.tip: Climb the 129 steps of the Pompejus lookout tower nearby for a view over the fort and the Brabantse Wal.

new.title: Hop across the border in Baarle-Nassau
new.desc: Baarle is a patchwork of Dutch and Belgian pieces, with Belgian enclaves inside the Netherlands and Dutch ones inside those. Rows of markers in the pavement show which country you are standing in.
new.tip: Find the house on Loveren where the border runs through the front door, giving it two house numbers.

new.title: Walk the fens of Oisterwijk
new.desc: Between Tilburg and Den Bosch, the Oisterwijkse Bossen en Vennen hide dozens of quiet forest fens, saved from development by Natuurmonumenten in 1913.
new.tip: Take the train to Oisterwijk and start at the visitor centre on the Van Tienhovenlaan; the marked routes pass a string of fens.
new.q: Bezoekerscentrum Oisterwijkse Bossen en Vennen Oisterwijk

new.title: Cross the bog on the log paths of De Groote Peel
new.desc: On the Brabant and Limburg border, this national park is a rare surviving piece of the raised bog that once covered the Peel, dug away for centuries for peat. Wooden walkways take you over the wettest parts.
new.tip: Walk the 3.2 km Knuppelbrug route from Buitencentrum De Pelen and stay on the paths: the peat can give way underfoot.

new.title: Look for beavers in the Biesbosch from Drimmelen
new.desc: The Biesbosch is one of Europe's largest freshwater tidal wetlands, a maze of creeks and willow forest where beavers and white-tailed eagles live.
new.tip: Rent a canoe or take a boat from the harbour of Drimmelen; the MuseumEiland has a roof you can walk on.

new.title: Cycle the glowing Starry Night path to Nuenen
new.desc: Daan Roosegaarde's cycle path between Eindhoven and Nuenen is set with thousands of glowing stones that light up after dark in swirls inspired by Van Gogh's The Starry Night.
new.tip: Ride it on a clear evening shortly after sunset, when the stones have soaked up the day's light; switch off your bike light for a moment.

fix.suggestion: Check evoluon.com / nextnature.org before keeping the museum claim; otherwise say it is a conference centre that opens for exhibitions and events.
